eyebrow: Quantum Error Correction & Fault Tolerance · Chapter 1
subtitle: Lesson 2 · Noise Models in Quantum Systems

eyebrow: Any single-qubit error reduces to three types

steps.label: A qubit's state lives in a 2D space spanned by |0⟩, |1⟩
steps.sub: A general state is α|0⟩ + β|1⟩

steps.label: A quantum error is any unwanted perturbation of that state
steps.sub: Environment noise, a stray pulse, a miscalibrated gate — anything unintended

steps.label: Remarkably, any single-qubit error decomposes into three types
steps.sub: Described by the three Pauli matrices: X, Y, and Z

steps.label: That's exactly what makes error correction possible at all
steps.sub: No need for a different correction scheme per physical noise source

caption: X is the quantum generalization of a classical bit flip — it swaps the two basis states.
Z leaves |0> and |1> individually alone but flips their relative sign — invisible to a computational-basis measurement.

steps.label: Y|0⟩ = i|1⟩, Y|1⟩ = −i|0⟩
steps.sub: Up to a phase factor of i, Y equals X and Z applied together

steps.label: A Y error is a bit-flip and phase-flip on the same qubit
This course's early codes target X and Z independently
steps.sub: A Y error is caught automatically as both occurring at once

steps.label: Any messy real noise decomposes into I, X, Y, Z
steps.sub: A code correcting X and Z, in principle, corrects any single-qubit error

subtitle: The standard textbook model for spreading an error budget evenly across X, Y, and Z.
